### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via admitAuthoredSource (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_ERROR (literal, 39 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `485db05709b0c270b4a4b7aebda1690e67ca1cbc` — the merge of head `0b2a3bc04739edf64097a7f23b8905b4cc05dc2a` into base `27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 485db05709b0c270b4a4b7aebda1690e67ca1cbc && git checkout 485db05709b0c270b4a4b7aebda1690e67ca1cbc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1 0b2a3bc04739edf64097a7f23b8905b4cc05dc2a && git checkout -B drift-repro 27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1 && git merge --no-ff 0b2a3bc04739edf64097a7f23b8905b4cc05dc2a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 27ee98438e61148e581b710e828bc51639361ff1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0b2a3bc04739edf64097a7f23b8905b4cc05dc2a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-refused-at-save.ts + packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-source-admission.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-save.dogfood.test.ts (the diff's paths outside the prose faces; the changeset and the two docs pages were read against the same code). Cited code read, not reviewed: packages/metadata-core/src/knowledge-source-save-admission.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations (types.ts, registry.ts.template, entries/README.md), packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts.

Inputs read: card #37961 (body and its three comments: triage 7227578818, claim 7227637048, dev report 7230978235), PR #38060 (body, file list, comments), the net diff from merge-base `8d34c4404f` to the head (7 files, +321 −5), and the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set change, one: a `knowledge_source` item whose `adapter` is a string that names no adapter registered on the running knowledge service is refused at `admitAuthoredSource`, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, before anything is written. Right, and it is the change the card orders (option A). The condition is `typeof authoredAdapter === 'string'` and not in `listAdapters()`, read at request time and never cached.
- Not moved, each confirmed in the code: an omitted `adapter` (the check needs a string; the unplaced check above it is unchanged); a mounted `adapter`; the system context (`ctx.isSystem` returns admitted on the first line, and `authoredKnowledgeSourceRefusal` returns before the service is asked); a source registered in code (`registerSource` does not call this function); `os validate` (no deployment, no service).
- Doors that inherit it, each a caller of `authoredKnowledgeSourceRefusal` and none edited here: REST `PUT /meta/:type/:name` (`meta-item-write-routes.ts`, passes `refused.code` through for any status but 403), the runtime dispatcher's `/meta` save (`meta.ts`, `deps.error(message, status)`, and 400 maps to `VALIDATION_ERROR` in `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`), the MCP `save_metadata_draft` (`mcp-authoring.ts`, keeps the code for any status but 403), and the package duplicate (`refuseDuplicatedKnowledgeSources`, refuses the whole duplicate with the status). The changeset, the docs and the entry name these four and no other. Right.
- Order inside the function, as the PR states and as the code reads: system admitted; no judgeable `source.object` admitted (left to the parse); no identity 403; unplaced 400; this check 400; no data engine 503; the gates. One existing fixture moved for that order (the no-engine case now mounts the adapter it names) and the test still pins the 503 it pinned. Right.
- Public surface: no export added or changed. `unmountedAdapterSaveText` is private. No schema change: `adapter` stays `z.string().optional()`. No new ADR-0112 code. Right.
- Timing claim in the hunk's comment ("a save is served after every store's start(), so the adapters registered now are the deployment's"): holds for the three shipped stores. `knowledge-memory` and `knowledge-pgvector` register in `start()` whether or not the store is healthy, and `knowledge-turso` registers in `start()` on all three paths, including a placeholder when the URL comes from settings, so a store that is mounted and down is not read as unmounted.
- `placeable` in `unmountedAdapterSaveText` mirrors rules 2 and 3 of `adapterIdFor` exactly (the deployment's adapter while registered, else the only adapter registered), so the remedy "leave `adapter` out" is offered only where an omitted adapter would be placed.
- Gate verdicts on the head: every check-run is success or skipped but `Test UI (1/16)` and its aggregate `Test UI`. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (which carries `check:adr-0087-registration`), `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core` 1 to 10 and `TypeScript Type Check` are green.
- The red, read from the log of job 140824439216 (attempt 2): one failure, `ui/scripts/__tests__/check-pending-changeset-literals.test.ts:172`, "3. the tree as it stands satisfies the rule, exits 0 through the CLI", `Test timed out in 15000ms`; Test Files 1 failed, 445 passed, 2 skipped (448); Tests 1 failed, 6075 passed. It is a timeout, not an assertion about the tree. Unrelated to this diff: the diff holds no path under `ui/`; the gate under test resolves its root to `ui/` and reads `ui/.changeset`, while this PR's changeset is in the repository root `.changeset`; and the same case timed out on `main` at `27ee98438e` (job 140796965590, cards #38072 and #38065) with none of this diff present. The head still carries a red check, so landing waits for #38072 or a green rerun; that is a queue fact, not a finding on this diff.
- The dogfood shards are skipped on a pull request by design (they run on the merge queue), so the new door pins in `knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-save.dogfood.test.ts` have not been run by any check-run on this head. Their evidence here is the dev's reported local battery; the queue build is the first gate verdict on them.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

- Changeset `.changeset/37961-knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-refused-at-save.md`: `@objectstack/service-knowledge` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind: a value an author could save is now refused. The kind takes at least minor on a package the diff moves, and both moved packages take minor. Right.
- Both declaration lines stand line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and they agree with the claim on the card.
- The breaking banner is present, with the FROM (a save that answered success), the TO (400, nothing written) and the one-line fix. Exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `registered knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-refused-at-save`, and the entry file of that id exists in the diff.
- What the changeset says is published matches what the diff publishes; it claims no schema change and there is none.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the dev report.
- Deviation 1 (no new error code; the sibling refusal's `VALIDATION_ERROR` with a message that names the source, the adapter and the mounted adapters): accepted. The card asks for a 400 that names the three; a new code would be a ledger change the card does not order.
- Deviation 2 (the no-engine fixture mounts `memory`): accepted, see ①.
- Deviations 3 to 5 are process notes with no effect on the tree.
- Out-of-scope note (the claim names `knowledge-source-admission.ts`; the function lives in `knowledge-service.ts`): confirmed on the head, no defect.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to push down.
- Semantic entry "number 19" against PR #38013, checked on purpose. The leading `19.` of an entry filename is the protocol major the entry registers under, not an ordinal: `main` already holds 16 entries named `19.*` under `entries/semantic/`. An entry is keyed by its `id`, the filename is derived from the id (`shardNameFor`, enforced by the generator), and the two ids differ: `knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-refused-at-save` here and `knowledge-source-save-refused-without-knowledge-service` there. So the two PRs add two different files. `registry.ts`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide are generated and git-ignored, so the two ids sorting next to each other meet in no committed file, and neither PR edits `registry.ts.template`. No test on `main` pins the count or the list of step-19 semantic ids. Verdict: no collision on the registry, in either landing order, and neither PR renames or renumbers anything.
- The two PRs do share two prose files. `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`: this PR rewrites base line 35; #38013 inserts after base line 42 and rewrites line 80. `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`: this PR rewrites base lines 169 to 170 and 233 to 234; #38013 rewrites 201 to 205 and inserts after 238. Every pair of hunks is separated by unchanged lines, so the text merge is clean by reading; this was read from the two diffs and not machine-merged, and the dev report records a clean overlap-check against #38013. The changesets have different names. #38013's tests use fake knowledge services, so this check does not reach them.
- What the second to land must change: if this PR lands second, nothing in its tree; the no-service 503 of #38013 answers before the knowledge service is reached, which is the order this PR's body already states. If #38013 lands second, one sentence it adds to the module doc of `knowledge-source-save-admission.ts` goes half-stale: it calls 503 "the code the knowledge service itself answers for a store that is not mounted", which after this PR is true at index and search and no longer at the save (400). That sentence should say where. Graded below as N4; it is owed by #38013, not by this head.
- Rule-level hardening note, graded N1 below: text taken from the saved item reaches a refusal message without the quoting and length bound this module applies to a caller-supplied name.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: the schema says `adapter` is an "adapter id, as an adapter registered it", and `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` on `main` says a named adapter that is not mounted is refused at index and search, 503. A source naming an unmounted adapter never indexed and never answered a search. So the change takes no working capability away at the consumer; it makes the spec's own refusal reach the author at the save. The one ordering it removes is "save the source first, mount its store later", and the refusal names that remedy (mount the store, then save again). The duplicate door now refuses a whole package that holds one such source, as it already did for an unplaced one; the changeset declares it.

The `hits` file, sentence by sentence against the code:
- `surface`: the four doors named are the four callers of `authoredKnowledgeSourceRefusal`. Holds.
- `replacement`: a mounted adapter id (the refusal lists them: holds), or no `adapter` (holds wherever an omitted adapter is placed; see N3), or mount the store first (holds).
- `reason`: stored before and refused 503 at index and search with a boot error (`reportUnmountedAdapters`, `getAdapter`: holds); now 400 naming the three, nothing written (holds; the doors return before the protocol is called); stored sources untouched (holds: no migration, no boot refusal, the boot reading is unchanged); package install, code registration and validate not judged (holds); no D2 conversion (holds: none is added, and none could choose the store).
- `acceptanceCriteria`: checkable by the consumer, and it is the pair of signals the code leaves (the boot's error line, and the save).
- Entry mechanics: filename equals `19.` plus the id plus `.ts`; the `id` line matches the generator's pattern; the initializer ends with `;`; the comment run above `export const entry` is the one carried into the registry; no call spelling in the prose. `relevantWhen` is omitted, which is right: the surface is a run-time save, not something that lives only under a top-level stack key, so the entry is always listed.
- It follows the precedent of `19.knowledge-source-publish-refuses-missing-references-and-gated-objects.ts`, which also added a step-19 notice without a rationale fragment in the template.

The implementing file, against the contract:
- The jsdoc added to `admitAuthoredSource` agrees with the hunk: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, names the source (through `describeName`, when the body carries a `name`), the adapter and the mounted ones; an omitted adapter is not refused; the system context, code registration and validate are outside this door.
- Attempts to break it: an empty-string adapter is refused (pinned); `adapter: null` or a number is left to the schema parse, which refuses it; zero adapters mounted names "none" and offers only the mount remedy (pinned); two adapters with no deployment mark does not offer "leave it out" (read in the code); a store that is mounted and unhealthy is still registered, so it is not refused; an author the field gate would refuse hears the adapter first (pinned), which discloses only the mounted adapter ids, to a caller who already passed the door's capability gates, as the unplaced refusal above it already does. None of these breaks the contract.
- The check sits after the early return for an item with no judgeable `source.object`, so such an item is not judged for its adapter here. That rests on the same assumption the existing gates rest on (the protocol's parse refuses the item), which the function's doc states; it is not new with this diff.

Tests in the diff: the unit cases drive the real `KnowledgeService` and pin the refusal for a retired, a mistyped and an empty adapter, the order before the field gate, the system bypass, the "none" and two-adapter lists, and three controls. The dogfood file pins the REST door and the MCP draft door on a booted showcase with a real token, with "nothing stored" read back at both, and controls at both. The changeset and the two docs pages agree with the code as read.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- N1 (nit) — rule level: a value taken from the unparsed item is interpolated into the refusal text without the JSON-quoting and 64-character bound that `quotedName` gives a caller-supplied name in this same module, and at the duplicate door that text was authored by someone other than the reader. Sibling refusals in the function already do the same with the object and field names, so this is the module's existing habit, not a regression. Follow-up card, not a fix on this head.
- N2 (nit) — the remedy branches of `unmountedAdapterSaveText` (the "leave `adapter` out" clause present with one adapter or a mounted deployment adapter, absent with two and no mark) are not asserted; the tests match only the rule half of the message. The duplicate door's answer for this refusal is likewise unpinned here and rests on the existing parity tests. Follow-up card.
- N3 (nit) — the entry's `replacement` offers "no `adapter` at all" without the qualifier the changeset carries: on a host that mounts several adapters and marks none the deployment's, an omitted adapter is itself refused 400, with its own prescription. The refusal text is conditional and correct; only the entry's sentence is unqualified. Accepted deviation or a follow-up; a fix in the entry file would move the reviewed head.
- N4 (nit) — owed by PR #38013 if it lands second, not by this head: scope its "the code the knowledge service itself answers for a store that is not mounted" sentence to index and search.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-o1C-37961`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czzx9dtSEm3jWWL9c3`

**VERDICT: PASS**

repo:objectstack#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czzx9dtSEm3jWWL9c3

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT on merits** at head `0b2a3bc04739edf64097a7f23b8905b4cc05dc2a` (Fixes #37961). Landing waits on one red check that is not this PR's.

## Review summary

**Contract review.** I adopt record 7232224061 at this head: PASS at the contract tier (`verify-review-tier` PASS), no must-fix, no should-fix, and four nits.
- The narrowing is the save refusing `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` when `adapter` names a store that is not mounted. It reaches the author at the save, where before the spec's existing refusal reached them only at index and search. It removes no working capability.
- The four doors named in the changeset, the docs and entry 19 are exactly the four callers of the predicate. Each is pinned.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, minor on both moved packages, the BREAKING banner with FROM, TO and the fix, and one ADR-0087 marker with its entry file are all right.

**Entry 19 and #38013.** The two PRs do not collide. `19.` is the protocol major, not an ordinal, and entries are keyed by id; the two ids differ. If #38013 lands second, one sentence it adds to the admission module's doc should say the save now answers `400` for an unmounted named store (N4 of the record). If this PR lands second, nothing changes.

**Dogfood.** The full battery is pinned to this head and green: 491 files passed, 3 skipped; 4148 tests passed, 68 skipped; no failures (7230978235). Dogfood shards do not run on a PR, so this run is the evidence.

**CI.** One red check: Test UI (1/16), `check-pending-changeset-literals` "exits 0 through the CLI", which times out at 15 s.
- It is main's flake #38072. The same case timed out on main (#38065).
- The diff has no `ui/**` path, and that gate reads `ui/.changeset`, not the root `.changeset`.
- It is unrelated, but the head still carries it. Landing waits for a green rerun or the #38072 fix.

**Nits, optional:**
- N1: route item-derived values in these refusals through the module's quoting helper. This is a follow-up, and the specifics go to the seat.
- N2: the remedy branches and the duplicate door's answer are not pinned.
- N3: the entry's `replacement` omits the qualifier on an omitted adapter.
- N4: the #38013 sentence above.

**Next:** this is a narrowing, so it goes to the seat for the Tier H approval. The PR is still a draft.

repo:objectstack#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cwoXEE1amuRAGHdPBs

Seat record · 2026-11-28T02:18Z · PR #38060 (Fixes #37961) · head `0b2a3bc04739edf64097a7f23b8905b4cc05dc2a` · `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — lands as Tier H

## 维护者速读

- 做什么：保存知识源时，如果它指定的存储（adapter）在当前部署里根本没挂载（比如已下线的 `ragflow`，或拼错），现在保存当场就被拒（400），并告诉作者有哪些可用的存储。以前是先存进去，启动时报错，之后每次建索引、搜索都回 503。
- 风险：7 个文件 +321/−5，集中在 service-knowledge 一处保存校验，加测试、dogfood 用例、两页文档和一条升级说明；对外是一处收窄（BREAKING，service-knowledge 和 spec 按 minor 发）。已经存着的知识源不受影响，包安装、种子数据、代码注册的知识源也不受影响。
- 要你做什么：审批人批准即可。契约审核 PASS 7232224061，Head-sha `0b2a3bc04739edf64097a7f23b8905b4cc05dc2a`；批准后座位自主落地。
- 不批会怎样：作者把存储名写错或写了已下线的存储，保存照样成功，问题要到搜索时才以 503 的形式冒出来，很难对上原因。

Seat opinion: land.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#1 · head `0b2a3bc047`

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, 7 files (+321/−5): `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts` (the save predicate) and its admission test, a new dogfood test, `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`, `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`, the migration entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-refused-at-save.ts`, and `.changeset/37961-knowledge-source-unmounted-adapter-refused-at-save.md` (minor on `@objectstack/service-knowledge` and `@objectstack/spec`, BREAKING banner with FROM, TO and the fix, one ADR-0087 marker). Body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 38060`: no governed path; the narrowing declaration routes it the Tier H way.
2. **Premise measured.** Per the records: the four doors named in the changeset (REST save, Studio, MCP `save_metadata_draft`, package duplicate) are the four callers of the predicate and each is pinned. Before, the save was stored and every index and search answered 503. A stored source is not touched. Card acceptance met.
3. **Gates (check-runs at this head).** 58 success, 10 skipped, 2 failed: `Test UI (1/16)` and its `Test UI` rollup, both the `check-pending-changeset-literals` "exits 0 through the CLI" 15 s timeout.
